info.title: Phantom AI
info.description: OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible model API with a routing model (phantom-1). Buy prepaid credit with Solana USDC over x402 or MPP at /v1/x402/top-up, then call any model with the API key it returns.
info.x-guidance: 1. POST /v1/x402/top-up with {"amount_usd": 1} (0.10 to 10000; an empty body buys $1). The unpaid request returns a 402 with x402 and MPP challenges for that amount in Solana USDC. Pay it and send the same request again; the response holds api_key (shown once), recovery_code and credit_usd. To add credit to a key you already hold, put it in the body as target_api_key, not in the Authorization header. 2. Call POST /v1/chat/completions (OpenAI shape), /v1/messages (Anthropic shape) or /v1/responses (OpenAI Responses shape) with Authorization: Bearer <api_key>. Streaming works. Each call is billed at its actual cost from the credit. Use model "phantom-1" to let the router pick, or any id from GET /v1/models.

post.description:
OpenAI's chat completions API, streaming or not. Phantom checks the key, runs its route policy (which picks the model for `model: "auto"`), estimates the prompt from the messages and tool definitions, and holds the worst-case cost on the key. It sets `max_tokens` to the output the hold covers, calls the upstream, and bills the cost the upstream reports in `usage.cost`, or the catalog rate for the reported tokens, at the rate of the model the upstream says it served. Every price includes Phantom's 5% markup on the Gateway's rate, the same rates `GET /v1/models` lists. A refused or failed call bills nothing and returns the hold.

A stream bills when it ends: finished, cut off by an error, or abandoned by you. When the usage frame never arrived, the prompt and output tokens fall back to estimates (about four characters per token, tool-call arguments included).

With the policy's `fallback_on_error` on, the upstream tries the policy's other models in the same call when the routed one fails. Phantom always asks the upstream to add prompt-cache markers where a provider needs them (`caching: "auto"`), and tries the cheapest provider of the model first (`sort: "cost"`) unless you set `sort`.

`sort`, `zdr` and `no_training` choose providers; the key's route policy can set them too, and the request wins.

parameters.name: x-phantom-session
parameters.description: Your own conversation id. With routing (`auto`, or a key's route policy), requests on the same key with the same id stay on the model picked for them while the policy's `stick_minutes` window lasts; `auto` on a key with no policy keeps it for the whole session. Only the first 200 characters count. Without it, the opening messages group requests instead. Phantom keeps this in server memory only, as a salted hash, and sends the upstream a hash of it under your key as `x-session-affinity`, so the same provider serves the session and its prompt cache stays warm.

parameters.name: x-phantom-agent
parameters.description: The coding agent a request came through: `claude-code`, `codex`, `cursor` or `coding-agent`. Phantom sets it when you call an agent's base path (`https://phantom.codes/codex/v1`), and tags the call with it at the upstream. Any other value is ignored.

parameters.name: x-phantom-route
parameters.description: Send `off` to skip the key's route policy for this request. The request runs on the model it names; `model: "auto"` is refused with a 400.

parameters.name: x-phantom-escalate
parameters.description: Send `1` when the current model isn't managing the task. Phantom Router moves the conversation one model up (free, then standard, then frontier) and keeps it there; a key's route policy moves it to the policy's last model. Phantom can't tell a weak answer from a good one, so escalation is your call.

parameters.name: x-phantom-free
parameters.description: Send `off` so Phantom Router doesn't pick its free model for this request. `zdr` or `no_training` turns it off too, since free models promise neither.

parameters.name: x-phantom-route-debug
parameters.description: Send `1` or `true` (or set `router_debug: true` in the request body) to return raw tier probability scores and selection threshold in `x-phantom-route-scores`.

requestBody.description: An OpenAI chat completions request. Fields not listed go to the upstream unchanged.

model.description: A chat model id from `GET /v1/models`; `phantom-1` to let Phantom Router pick its free, standard or frontier model per task; or `auto` to route by the key's route policy (Phantom Router when the key has none). Renamed ids resolve to the current one. `phantom-1` with an image runs `alibaba/qwen3.7-flash`.

stream.description: Answer as a server-sent event stream.

stream_options.description: Passed through, with `include_usage` forced to `true` on streams so the usage frame always arrives.

max_tokens.description: Your output limit. Phantom sends the smallest of this, what the balance buys after the prompt, and the model's output cap, shrunk to what the hold covers.

max_completion_tokens.description: Read before `max_tokens` when both are set. When sent, Phantom replaces it with the same limit it sends as `max_tokens`.

n.description: Always sent as 1. One completion per request.

tools.description: Tool definitions. Count toward the prompt estimate.

functions.description: Legacy function definitions. Count toward the prompt estimate.

sort.description: How to rank the providers that serve the model before trying them: `cost` (cheapest first, the default), `ttft` (fastest first token) or `tps` (most tokens per second). Overrides the key's route policy. Phantom removes it before calling the upstream.

zdr.description: Only use providers that delete prompts right away (zero data retention). Not available yet: a request with `zdr: true` gets 403 `zdr_unavailable`. Phantom removes it before calling the upstream.

no_training.description: Only use providers that don't train on prompts. Phantom removes it before calling the upstream.

provider.description: The upstream's shorthand for provider routing, such as `{"sort": "tps"}`, passed through unchanged. When it sets `sort`, Phantom sends no default sort.

providerOptions.description: Passed to the upstream, except `gateway.models`, which Phantom replaces with the policy's fallbacks or drops. `gateway.order` still chooses among providers of the same model. Your `gateway` settings win over `sort`, `zdr` and `no_training`. `order` (providers to try first), `only` (the only providers allowed) and `sort` all pass through.

model.description: The model the upstream reports running. Billing uses this model's rate when the catalog carries it.

usage.description: What Phantom bills from. When the token counts are missing, Phantom estimates them.

cost.description: What the upstream charged, in US dollars. Billed as-is unless it is more than 100 times the catalog price.

phantom.description: Added by Phantom: what this call cost and how it was served.

cost_usd.description: What this call was charged, in US dollars. Same as `x-phantom-cost-usd`.

provider.description: The provider that answered, or null when the upstream did not say.

attempts.description: Provider attempts across every model tried. 1 when the first try worked.

fallback.description: `true` when a provider or model failed and another one answered.

schema.description: With `stream: true`: the upstream's `data: {chunk}` lines, passed through, ending with `data: [DONE]`. Just before the chunk that holds `data: [DONE]`, Phantom inserts `event: phantom.receipt` with `data: {"receipt":"<compact receipt>","phantom":{...}}`, where `phantom` has the same fields as in a non-streaming answer. That receipt's `output_hash` covers the text you received. Without a signing key the event carries `phantom` only.

x-phantom-content-logged.description: Always `false`: Phantom did not store the prompt or the output of this call. Also sent with a passed-through upstream error.

x-phantom-routed.description: Present when Phantom picked the model, either Phantom Router for `phantom-1` or the key's route policy for `auto`: the model id, then `; reason=` and what decided it. A rule shows as `<condition>:<value>`; other reasons are `default` (the policy's first model), `requested`, `cache` (kept on the conversation's model) and `on_empty` (past the budget, the cheapest model). Also sent with a passed-through upstream error.

x-phantom-route-receipt.description: Sent on routed `phantom-1` calls: names requested model, served tier, underlying model, calibrated confidence, routing reason, and estimated percentage savings. Sent on routed phantom-1 calls: names requested model, served tier, underlying model, calibrated confidence, reason, and estimated percentage savings.

x-phantom-route-scores.description: Returns raw tier probability scores, selected tier, and threshold when debug mode is requested via `x-phantom-route-debug: 1` or `router_debug: true`. Sent when x-phantom-route-debug: 1 or router_debug: true is requested: returns tier scores, selected tier, and threshold.

x-phantom-upstream.description: Always `pai`. The receipt's `upstream` field holds the same value. Always `pai`. Also sent with a passed-through upstream error.

x-phantom-upstream-model.description: The model id Phantom sent to the upstream. On chat and messages, the receipt's `model_served` holds the id the upstream reported running. Also sent with a passed-through upstream error.

x-phantom-upstream-request-id.description: The upstream's own request id, copied from its `x-request-id` response header when it sends one. Also sent with a passed-through upstream error.

x-phantom-receipt.description: A signed receipt for the call: `base64url(canonical JSON payload).base64url(Ed25519 signature)`. The payload names the model served, token counts, cost and hashes of the request and response. Check it against `GET /v1/receipts/key`. Left out when the deployment has no signing key. Non-streaming answers only. `model_requested` is the id you sent after renames (`auto` stays `auto`), `model_served` is the `model` field of the upstream's answer, and `reasoning_tokens` comes from `usage.completion_tokens_details`. A stream carries the receipt in the body instead.

x-phantom-cached-tokens.description: Prompt tokens the upstream served from its cache, billed at the cached rate. Non-streaming answers only.

x-phantom-cost-usd.description: What this call was charged, in US dollars. Non-streaming answers only. A stream carries it in the `phantom.receipt` event.

x-phantom-provider.description: The provider that answered, such as `anthropic`, `bedrock` or `azure`. Left out when the upstream does not say. Non-streaming answers only.

x-phantom-fallback.description: `true` when a provider or model failed and another one answered the call, `false` when the first try worked. Non-streaming answers only.

x-phantom-balance-usd.description: Credit left on the key after this call was billed, in US dollars. Left out when the debit found no key to charge; never sent as a guessed zero. Non-streaming answers only. A stream's headers leave before it is billed.

cache-control.description: Caching rules for the response. Streams only: `no-cache`.

400.description: The body is not JSON, `sort`, `zdr` or `no_training` has a bad value (`invalid_prefs`), or the route policy could not route (`route_required`: `auto` with `x-phantom-route: off`, or no model in the policy can take the request), or a paid request without `stream: true` (`stream_required`).

401.description: No `Bearer` key (`missing_api_key`), a key Phantom does not know (`invalid_api_key`), or an expired or deactivated key (`api_key_expired`).

402.description: The key is past its spend cap and its policy did not move the request to its cheapest model (`budget_exceeded`), or it holds less than $0.001, cannot pay for the prompt alone, cannot buy 32 output tokens after it, or the hold failed (`insufficient_quota`).

403.description: The request asked for `zdr`, which is not available yet (`zdr_unavailable`). Nothing is billed.

404.description: The model is not a chat model in the catalog (`model_not_found`), or it was retired (`model_retired`, which names the closest current model).

429.description: The key's per-minute spend cap is reached (`spend_rate_exceeded`).

retry-after.description: Seconds to wait before trying again. Sent when the key's per-minute spend cap is reached.

502.description: Phantom has no upstream key configured, or the upstream could not be reached. Nothing is billed.

parameters.name: x-phantom-session
parameters.description: Your own conversation id. With routing (`auto`, or a key's route policy), requests on the same key with the same id stay on the model picked for them while the policy's `stick_minutes` window lasts; `auto` on a key with no policy keeps it for the whole session. Phantom Router moves the conversation one model up (free, then standard, then frontier) and keeps it there; a key's route policy moves it to the policy's last model. post.summary: Fetch a key again with its recovery code
post.description: Returns the key a paid purchase issued, given the recovery code shown at checkout. Needs no payment id and does not expire; it works for as long as the payment row exists. If the key was never handed out, this call creates it. An unknown code and an unpaid payment get the same answer, so the route does not reveal which codes exist. Needs no API key.

get.summary: Get a top-up's status and its key once paid
get.description:
Reports where a purchase stands and, once it is paid, hands back the key. For a Solana payment each poll also looks for the transfer on chain (at most every few seconds per server) and marks the payment paid when a transfer with the reference, at least the owed amount and a time inside the quote window plus a short grace has landed. A card payment is marked paid by Stripe's webhook.

A paid purchase that named a key credits that key and extends its expiry to at least the new validity; no key comes back. Otherwise the new key is sealed with the recovery code, so send `x-phantom-recovery-code` to get it. The first poll with the code creates the key; later polls with the code return the same key. Needs no API key. This route is left out of the purchase rate limit.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The `payment_id` from the purchase call.

parameters.name: x-phantom-recovery-code
parameters.description: The recovery code shown at checkout. With it, the status poll decrypts and returns the key of a paid purchase. Sent as a header so it never lands in a URL or access log. Without it, a paid purchase that issues a new key reports `ready` and `recovery_required: true`, and no key.

200.description: The purchase's state.

status.description: `pending` until paid; `ready` when paid but the key was not handed out on this poll; `completed` when this poll returned the key or the top-up landed; `expired` when the daily cleanup job marked a payment still pending after 7 days. A Solana transfer that lands later can still move an expired payment to paid. `confirming` appears only on old rows.

api_key.description: The new key, when the purchase is paid and the recovery code opened it. Left out otherwise.

topped_up.description: The credit landed on the key named at checkout. No `api_key` comes back in that case.

recovery_required.description: The payment needs its recovery code to hand out a key, and none came back on this poll. True while the payment is unpaid too. Always false for a top-up, which lands on a key you already hold.

credit_usd.description: Credit the purchase adds, in US dollars.

expires_at.description: When the payment itself expires if unpaid. Not the key's expiry.

pay_currency.description: For a Solana payment, the coin: `sol`, `usdcsol` or `usdtsol`. `null` for a card payment.

pay_amount.description: For a Solana payment, the exact amount owed in whole coins. `null` for a card payment.

400.description: No payment id in the path.

post.summary: Create a Solana anchor for a receipt for $0.01
post.description: Writes the SHA-256 of a receipt to Solana in a memo transaction, so anyone can later see it existed at that time. Phantom first checks the receipt against its own signing key and refuses one it did not sign, before reading your key. The charge is `RECEIPT_ANCHOR_COST_MICRO` in lib/config.ts ($0.01), taken after the transaction confirms; a transaction that does not land costs nothing. A receipt anchored before is answered from the record at no charge, though the key must still be able to pay the fee to get that far.

200.description: The receipt is anchored, now or earlier.

already_anchored.description: `true` when an earlier call anchored this receipt; nothing was charged.

leaf_hash.description: SHA-256 hex of the compact receipt, exactly as held.

tx_signature.description: The Solana transaction that carries the hash in a memo.

slot.description: The Solana slot the transaction landed in, when known.

explorer_url.description: The transaction on Solana Explorer, for the network this deployment uses.

x-phantom-cost-usd.description: What this call was charged, in US dollars. The anchoring fee. Not sent for a repeat anchor.

x-phantom-balance-usd.description: Credit left on the key after this call was billed, in US dollars. Left out when the debit found no key to charge; never sent as a guessed zero. Not sent for a repeat anchor.
